name: What Is the Difference Between a Written Estimate and a Fixed-Price Remodeling Contract?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a written kitchen remodeling estimate and a fixed-price contract when comparing contractor proposals?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a written kitchen remodeling estimate and a fixed-price contract when comparing contractor proposals?

acceptedAnswer.text: A written estimate is often a proposal used to describe anticipated work and pricing. A fixed-price contract generally establishes an agreed price for a defined scope, but it may still contain allowances, exclusions, provisional items, material adjustments, and change-order provisions. The document’s title matters less than its terms. Ask the contractor to identify the scope included in the base price, each allowance, unit price, exclusion, price-validity period, and condition that permits an adjustment. Confirm whether permits, design, delivery, disposal, inspections, hidden conditions, owner selections, and supplier increases are included or separately priced. Review how additions, deletions, substitutions, and credits are approved. Before signing, ensure the written agreement incorporates the final estimate, drawings, selections, schedule, payment plan, warranty, and completion requirements. If a proposal says “estimate only,” ask what document will control pricing and when it becomes effective. Do not assume that a detailed estimate is fixed simply because it has a total. Understanding the difference helps homeowners compare actual financial commitments rather than preliminary numbers.
acceptedAnswer.description: A written estimate describes expected scope and cost, while a fixed-price contract states the agreed price for defined work, subject to listed allowances, exclusions, and approved changes. Ask when the estimate becomes binding and which conditions can change the final amount.
